changes_from_r1: frame: no two faces that face the same way lie in one plane and overlap (checks.coplanar_frame; r1 had 492 such pairs: the iron band tops lay in the end-grain plane of the post tops, the sill band under its plates, neighbouring stave tops and bottoms, the plate/band edge). Fixed in geometry: bands end 4 mm below the post heads, the sill band runs between the plates, every other stave stands 4 mm lower, plates sink 1.5 mm into the beam they sit on, beams, boards and studs run 2 mm into the post, deck or wall they meet.
arrows and bolts stand as bundles: each unit's copies together in their own spot (no cord); same unit count and groups
bomb crate: 4 bombs per unit (16 per half, r1: 8), settled as a heap, so a full half reads full

frame.stacking: not stackable: the arrow sheaves stand above the frame (to ~1.5 m); keep this store out of the flat-top stacking rule in BuildPiece (it is a ground store).

space.unity: prefab space, origin on the floor at the centre of the footprint, +z front, +y up, +x to the furniture's left seen from the front

groups.0-5: arrow barrels, left to right seen from the front (8 units each)
groups.6-7: bolt tubs, front left (4 units each)
groups.8-9: bomb crate halves, front right (4 units each)
groups.rule: one item kind per group (StoreModel.ByGroup). Each unit's 'kind' (arrow / bolt / bomb) names the family its copies are packed for. ByGroup itself does not look at it: a stack claims the free group nearest to its chest-grid spot, so an arrow stack can claim a bolt tub or the crate (drawn as an 0.86 m arrow standing in a tub or among the bombs). A family filter in ByGroup (like the existing egg-and-hook rule: ammo type -> unit kind) keeps them apart.

fill_order: units are listed group by group; inside a group in fill order: step 0 is the core of the sheaf (barrel and tub centre, the crate's back row), later steps stand round it, so the bundle thickens as stock grows. ByGroup dequeues a group's units in this order.
position: unit position = mean of its copies' feet, on the floor of its holder (barrel and tub heads at y 0.215, the straw peaks at y 0.219). box = [x, y, z] Unity, informational.
copy_rule: arrows and bolts: align (long axis -> up, thin axis -> x), then_rotate = a lean of up to 4 degrees (5 for bolts) times a spin about the shaft, fit_longest_m (arrows 0.86, bolts 0.32), anchor bottom. Bombs: no align, rot_quat_xyzw (any spin, up to 10 degrees of tilt), fit_longest_m 0.22, anchor bottom. offset.y = the copy's foot height in the straw (arrows 0 .. 0.42 in steps of 0.07, bolts 0 .. 0.08) plus the lift that keeps the lowest vertex of every model of the family above it (a leaning copy dips below its bounds). Bombs: 4 per unit, 16 per half, dropped and settled one by one (a heap that rises over the rim when full).
straw: barrels and tubs are packed with straw to 0.45 (arrows) and 0.11 (bolts) over the head; every foot stands in it. The straw surface is part of the frame, with each triangle that any copy of any model touches cut away, so the straw parts round the shafts and nothing clips it.

heads.why: Align.Axes turns the item's +long axis to up; the arrow models differ in sign (flint's head is at item +z, poison's at -z), so no single anchor stands every kind head-up. A per-prefab half turn in C# (like the Greens table) for the four 'down' kinds would make all of them head-up.

items.arrow_size: an arrow item is 1.63-1.84 m long in the game (ArrowFlint: root scale 1, child 'model' scale 1.5 on a 1.144 m mesh; mod bounds 0.176 x 0.302 x 1.839). Here: fit_longest_m 0.86 = 0.47x flint, a real arrow's length; at 0.70x a barrel held only 2-5 arrows without touching (the carapace and silver models are 0.24 m across).

not_checked.ArrowNeedle: two Quad renderers from Unity's built-in resources (not in the bundle, not ripped); its mesh is 1.82 m like the others

layout.bundles: each unit's copies stand as one bundle in its own spot: the shafts pass the gather height (arrows 0.66 m, bolts 0.25 m over the head) within 5 cm (bolts 10 cm) of the bundle centre and lean a few degrees apart there, so heads and fletchings open out a little; no cord (the straw packing shows they were bundled by hand).

checks.method: mesh against mesh (BVH): every copy of every checked model against the frame and against every other copy in its group; the full render fill also across groups.
